routes.label: Use symmetry and the logarithm of a product

question: What is the product of all real numbers \(x\) such that the distance on the number line between \(\log_6 x\) and \(\log_6 9\) is twice the distance on the number line between \(\log_6 10\) and \(1?\)
solution:
The two possible logarithms lie equally far on opposite sides of \(\log_6 9\), so their sum can be found without calculating the distance.

We require \(x>0\) for \(\log_6 x\) to exist. Let
\[
d=2|\log_6 10-1|.
\]
Since \(10>6\), we have \(\log_6 10>1\), so \(d>0\). There are exactly two logarithm values at distance \(d\) from \(\log_6 9\). Let their corresponding positive values of \(x\) be \(a\) and \(b\). Then
\[
\log_6 a=\log_6 9-d,
\qquad
\log_6 b=\log_6 9+d.
\]
Each logarithm value determines exactly one positive number, so these are all the solutions. Adding the equations and using the logarithm product rule gives
\[
\log_6(ab)=2\log_6 9=\log_6 81.
\]
Therefore their product is \(\boxed{81}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
A distance on the number line is the absolute value of a difference, which lets us translate the condition into two logarithmic equations.

The logarithm requires \(x>0\). Since \(10>6\), the fixed distance is
\[
|\log_6 10-1|
=\log_6 10-\log_6 6
=\log_6\frac53.
\]
Twice this distance is
\[
2\log_6\frac53=\log_6\frac{25}{9}.
\]
Thus the required equation becomes
\[
\left|\log_6\frac{x}{9}\right|
=\log_6\frac{25}{9}.
\]
The right side is positive, so there are exactly two branches:
\[
\log_6\frac{x}{9}=\log_6\frac{25}{9}
\quad\text{or}\quad
\log_6\frac{x}{9}=-\log_6\frac{25}{9}
=\log_6\frac9{25}.
\]
Equality of logarithms gives
\[
\frac{x}{9}=\frac{25}{9}
\quad\text{or}\quad
\frac{x}{9}=\frac9{25}.
\]
Hence the two solutions are \(25\) and \(81/25\), both positive. Their product is
\[
25\cdot\frac{81}{25}=\boxed{81},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
